backend.topology: one JuiceFS volume: SQLite metadata engine + local file object store; two independent client processes in two containers, each mounting through JuiceFS's own FUSE client
backend.object_store: file:///jfs/obj (key/value object layout on a host bind mount)
backend.format_options: --storage file --bucket /jfs/obj --block-size 16384 (KiB; JuiceFS maximum, its default is 4096 KiB) --trash-days 0 --compress none

mount_options.why: --cache-size 1 MiB makes the client data cache negligible so the cold-restore column is not served by a JuiceFS client cache; --open-cache 0 keeps the documented close-to-open default; attribute and entry caches stay at their 1 s defaults

backend.label: SINGLE HOST, one volume, TWO client processes, one writer at a time. Not a fleet, not multi-node, not clustered performance, not a cloud result. The object store and the SQLite database are host directories, so no media or power-loss claim is made.

container.why_capabilities: the JuiceFS client mounts through /dev/fuse; SYS_ADMIN is the minimum mount capability
lost_capabilities_observed: CAP_SYS_RESOURCE absent: JuiceFS logs 'CAP_SYS_RESOURCE is needed for PR_SET_IO_FLUSHER'; the client runs without IO-flusher priority protection
setpriority denied: JuiceFS logs 'setpriority: permission denied'; no in-client priority tuning

arms.label: full
arms.durability: JuiceFS write-back mode is off (the default): a completed write has its data uploaded to the file object store and its metadata committed in SQLite, after an fsync of the file (A-E) or of the atomic metadata file (N).

close_to_open.method: writer does dd conv=fsync (data + metadata durable), the peer polls a fresh open+read for a matching SHA-256 at 10 ms resolution; the recorded value is a ceiling on visibility latency

in_place_rewrite.method: A replaces the file atomically; B polls head -c 17 until it sees the new prefix
in_place_rewrite.why: JuiceFS guarantees close-to-open consistency, not read-after-write; the attribute/entry cache is 1 s by default and is recorded in the mount options

n_client_failure.method: client A writes 1 MiB chunks, each sync(2)-ed and its SHA-256 acknowledged to a container-local log, until the write fails; client A's JuiceFS processes are SIGKILLed mid-write; client B then reads every acknowledged chunk; a fresh client A mounts the same volume and reads them again
n_client_failure.kill: SIGKILL of every JuiceFS process in client A while the writer was still running; acknowledged-before-kill=8 acknowledged-final=9 write-failed-at-chunk=10
n_client_failure.rule: every acknowledged (fsynced) chunk must read back intact on the peer; bytes beyond the last acknowledgement are unacknowledged and are reported, not counted as a loss

non_claims: one host, one volume, two client processes, one writer at a time; not a fleet, cluster or multi-node result
SQLite metadata engine; not the Redis/PostgreSQL/MariaDB/TiKV engines, and not the JuiceFS cloud service
local file object store; not S3/GCS/Azure object storage over a network
no media, power-loss or host-cache-loss claim; the failure test kills client processes, not a machine or a disk
no claim about JuiceFS versions other than the pinned release recorded here
